tools.name: commsharbor_health
tools.description: Read deployment health and build. Smoke tests wait for their own commit to appear here instead of racing edge propagation.

tools.name: commsharbor_logout
tools.description: Revoke the current session. Bootstrap/CSRF must belong to this browser and session. Other product sessions remain active.

tools.name: commsharbor_me
tools.description: Read the current account profile and platform role. `user.id` is the shared-account ID. Organizations are not listed here: they live in the shared account, which does not list them inside products yet — open a workspace by its ID with `GET /api/organizations/{organization_id}`.

tools.name: commsharbor_context
tools.description: Resolve the active organization identity. Read this before a write when you are not certain which tenant is active. Guessing is how data lands in the wrong organization. An organization API key answers `kind: api_key` with its scopes.

tools.name: commsharbor_organization_get
tools.description: Open an organization by id: name, your role and the CommsHarbor plan. This is how a workspace is opened. Name and role come from the shared account (null with an organization API key, which carries neither); the plan is the organization's global entitlement in CommsHarbor.

tools.name: commsharbor_audit
tools.description: List tenant audit events. Audit records are never rewritten and never carry recipient PII.

tools.name: commsharbor_platform_context
tools.description: Confirm the caller's platform role. Tenant ownership grants nothing here: platform access is a separate, explicit grant.

tools.name: commsharbor_domains
tools.description: List sending domains with their last observed state. `status` is what was last OBSERVED at SES and DNS. It does not become `active` because provisioning was requested.

tools.name: commsharbor_domain_create
tools.description: Register the organization's exact sending domain and queue SES provisioning. Asking twice does not provision twice. Publish the returned DKIM records, then call `verify` to have the state observed.

tools.name: commsharbor_domain_get
tools.description: Read one stored sending-domain resource. This returns what was stored at the last observation. To look again, call `verify`.

tools.name: commsharbor_domain_verify
tools.description: Refresh domain readiness from real SES and DNS observations. This is the ONLY operation that can move a domain to `active`, and only because it actually looked.

tools.name: commsharbor_domain_smoke
tools.description: Send one controlled smoke to the server-side recipient secret; never accepts a recipient argument. The request never accepts a recipient: the destination is a server-side secret. That is what keeps this from becoming a way to send mail to arbitrary addresses through someone else's verified domain.

tools.name: commsharbor_domain_deliveries
tools.description: List a domain's deliveries without recipient addresses.

tools.name: commsharbor_delivery_get
tools.description: Read one delivery and its SES MessageId without recipient data. `ses_message_id` is what correlates this record with AWS when you need to chase a message there.

tools.name: commsharbor_delivery_events
tools.description: List normalized SES feedback events for one delivery. Open and Click are ADDITIVE: they are recorded alongside delivery state and never overwrite it.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_contacts_list
tools.description: Lists contacts in the tenant CRM — a person in the tenant CRM. Cursor-paginated: limit 1-100, opaque cursor from the previous page. Filters: q, company_id. Needs crm:read on the organization. Every item carries an absolute url. Being in the CRM is not permission to email: consent lives in the `marke

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_contacts_create
tools.description: Creates a contact in the tenant CRM. Required: email, first_name. Needs crm:write on the organization. Returns the created resource with its absolute url. Being in the CRM is not permission to email: consent lives in the `marketing` sub-resource.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_contacts_get
tools.description: Reads one contact from the tenant CRM. Needs crm:read on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404. Being in the CRM is not permission to email: consent lives in the `marketing` sub-resource.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_contacts_update
tools.description: Updates one contact in the tenant CRM; only the fields you send change. Needs crm:write on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404. Being in the CRM is not permission to email: consent lives in the `marketing` sub-resource.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_contacts_delete
tools.description: Deletes one contact from the tenant CRM. Needs crm:write on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404. Being in the CRM is not permission to email: consent lives in the `marketing` sub-resource.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_companies_list
tools.description: Lists companies in the tenant CRM — an organization in the tenant CRM — a customer of the customer. Cursor-paginated: limit 1-100, opaque cursor from the previous page. Filters: q. Needs crm:read on the organization. Every item carries an absolute url.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_companies_create
tools.description: Creates a company in the tenant CRM. Required: name. Needs crm:write on the organization. Returns the created resource with its absolute url.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_companies_get
tools.description: Reads one company from the tenant CRM. Needs crm:read on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_companies_update
tools.description: Updates one company in the tenant CRM; only the fields you send change. Needs crm:write on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_companies_delete
tools.description: Deletes one company from the tenant CRM. Needs crm:write on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_pipelines_get

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_pipelines_delete

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_deals_create

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_deals_get

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_deals_delete
tools.description: Deletes one deal from the tenant CRM. Needs crm:write on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404. Money is in minor units: `value_minor: 10000` with `currency: "USD"` is $100.00, not $10,000.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_activities_list
tools.description: Lists activities in the tenant CRM — something that happened with a contact, company or deal. Cursor-paginated: limit 1-100, opaque cursor from the previous page. Filters: q, deal_id, contact_id, company_id, activity_type. Needs crm:read on the organization. Every item carries an absolute url.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_activities_create
tools.description: Creates a activity in the tenant CRM. Required: note. Needs crm:write on the organization. Returns the created resource with its absolute url.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_activities_get
tools.description: Reads one activity from the tenant CRM. Needs crm:read on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_activities_update
tools.description: Updates one activity in the tenant CRM; only the fields you send change. Needs crm:write on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_activities_delete
tools.description: Deletes one activity from the tenant CRM. Needs crm:write on the organization. A foreign or missing id answers 404.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_tasks_list

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_tasks_create
tools.description: Creates a task in the tenant CRM. Required: title. Needs crm:write on the organization. Returns the created resource with its absolute url.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_tasks_get

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_stages_list
tools.description: Lists stages in the tenant CRM — one step of a pipeline, addressed under the pipeline it belongs to. Cursor-paginated: limit 1-100, opaque cursor from the previous page. Needs crm:read on the organization. Every item carries an absolute url.

tools.name: commsharbor_crm_stages_create

tools.description: Lists leads in the platform CRM — a prospective ORGANIZATION in our own funnel — platform CRM is not tenant data. tools.name: commsharbor_platform_crm_leads_get

tools.name: commsharbor_platform_crm_leads_update

tools.name: commsharbor_platform_crm_activities_create
tools.description: Creates a activity in the platform CRM. Required: note. Needs a human session with the platform_admin grant; tenant ownership does not qualify. Returns the created resource with its absolute url.

tools.name: commsharbor_contact_marketing_get
tools.description: Read consent and preference for a CRM contact. Being in the CRM is not permission to email. This resource is where permission actually lives.

tools.name: commsharbor_contact_marketing_put
tools.description: Record permission-based marketing consent. This NEVER restores a previous unsubscribe. If the contact opted out, they stay out and `marketing_enabled` remains false — recording consent after the fact does not undo their decision.

tools.name: commsharbor_preference_token_create
tools.description: Create signed preference and unsubscribe URLs. The capability is scoped to one organization and one contact, it expires, and it embeds no email address. Put `marketing_headers` in the message and the unsubscribe works without a login.

tools.name: commsharbor_preference_get
tools.description: Read preference through a signed capability. The token IS the credential. It reveals preference state and nothing else — no email address, no CRM record.

tools.name: commsharbor_preference_unsubscribe
tools.description: Apply one-click unsubscribe through a signed capability. This is the endpoint mail clients call from the `List-Unsubscribe-Post` header, which is why the body is form-encoded and fixed. Calling it twice is the same as calling it once.

tools.name: commsharbor_marketing_smoke
tools.description: Send one controlled permission-based marketing smoke. Like the transactional smoke, the destination is a server-side secret. `contact_id` must be the CRM contact that matches it — you cannot point this at an arbitrary person.

tools.name: commsharbor_contact_imports
tools.description: List the contact imports of the organization.

tools.name: commsharbor_contact_import_preview
tools.description: Upload and preview a consent-declared CSV. Nothing is created by this call. The consent declaration is mandatory: an import that cannot say why these people may be emailed is an import that does not happen.

tools.name: commsharbor_contact_import_get
tools.description: Read one durable contact import and its current counts.

tools.name: commsharbor_contact_import_confirm
tools.description: Confirm an import with a mandatory idempotency key. The idempotency key is mandatory here. Reusing it returns the same import and never creates a second Queue message — which is what keeps a retry from importing everyone twice.

tools.name: commsharbor_contact_import_errors
tools.description: List the row-numbered errors of one import, so the source file can be fixed.

tools.name: commsharbor_contact_file_get
tools.description: Download a tenant CSV before expiry. Files expire seven days after creation. Durable audit and row-level results survive the file.

tools.name: commsharbor_contacts_export
tools.description: Create a CSV export of the organization's contacts, retained for seven days.

tools.name: commsharbor_suppressions
tools.description: List organization suppressions. Global, organization and SES tenant suppressions are all checked BEFORE quota and before any queue work.

tools.name: commsharbor_suppression_create
tools.description: Suppress one recipient inside the active organization.

tools.name: commsharbor_audiences
tools.description: List static audiences and saved segments.

tools.name: commsharbor_audience_create
tools.description: Create an audience or saved segment. Only allowlisted filter fields are accepted — a saved segment cannot be turned into an arbitrary query over the CRM.

tools.name: commsharbor_audience_get
tools.description: Read one audience of this organization.

tools.name: commsharbor_audience_update
tools.description: Rename an audience or change its saved filter.

tools.name: commsharbor_audience_delete
tools.description: Delete an audience and its memberships. Contacts themselves are untouched.

tools.name: commsharbor_audience_members
tools.description: List the contacts currently in one audience.

tools.name: commsharbor_audience_member_add
tools.description: Add a CRM contact to a static audience. Only for `static` audiences: a saved segment's membership comes from its filter, not from this route.

tools.name: commsharbor_audience_member_remove
tools.description: Remove a contact from a static audience.

tools.name: commsharbor_templates
tools.description: List the versioned email templates of the organization.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_create
tools.description: Create a canonical block template draft. Creating never publishes. Nothing can send this template until `publish` freezes a version.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_get
tools.description: Read one template draft owned by this organization.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_update
tools.description: Update one template draft. Editing a draft can never change what a past delivery rendered: published versions are immutable.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_archive
tools.description: Archive a template and preserve its versions. Deliveries that referenced a version must keep resolving to it, so archiving hides the draft and keeps the history.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_publish
tools.description: Publish an immutable template version. The version's identity is the hash of its compiled content — publishing identical content does not create a second version.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_versions
tools.description: List the immutable published versions of a template.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_preview
tools.description: Compile and render a safe template preview. `warnings` tells you what was stripped and what would not render — read it before publishing rather than after sending.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_export
tools.description: Export the latest published HTML, text and MJML.

tools.name: commsharbor_template_import_html
tools.description: Import a safe HTML subset as a draft. Active content, forms and unsafe URLs are rejected, not sanitised-and-kept. What survives is stored as blocks, so an imported template behaves exactly like an authored one.

tools.name: commsharbor_message_send
tools.description: Queue one idempotent transactional delivery. Same behaviour and same idempotency as `POST /api/messages`. `X-Organization-Id` is still required with the session and must match the path. Prefer the canonical route.

tools.name: commsharbor_campaigns
tools.description: List the campaigns of the organization.

tools.name: commsharbor_campaign_create
tools.description: Create a campaign draft. All three must already exist and be usable: a draft cannot be created against an unverified domain or an unpublished template.

tools.name: commsharbor_campaign_get
tools.description: Read one campaign, without any recipient data.

tools.name: commsharbor_campaign_update
tools.description: Edit, pause, resume or cancel a campaign. Content can only change while the campaign is a draft. After launch this route moves state — the frozen recipient set and the frozen template version do not change.

tools.name: commsharbor_campaign_launch
tools.description: Freeze and launch or schedule a campaign idempotently. The freeze happens once and never again: consent, suppressions and audience membership are evaluated at this moment, and the resulting set is what gets sent. Replaying the same Idempotency-Key returns the same campaign and produces no second dis

tools.name: commsharbor_campaign_report
tools.description: Reconcile campaign deliveries and feedback. Counts only. Which specific person opened what is not something this API answers.

tools.name: commsharbor_messaging_settings
tools.description: Read the organization's timezone and whether marketing is currently paused.

tools.name: commsharbor_messaging_settings_update
tools.description: Update timezone or pause state. Pausing is always allowed. Resuming is not: if the pause came from reputation or SES tenant risk, a healthy observation has to exist first.

tools.name: commsharbor_deliverability
tools.description: Read deliverability and backlog aggregates. This is the operator's single view of whether sending is healthy. It carries no recipient PII.

tools.name: commsharbor_domain_report
tools.description: Read domain delivery and feedback aggregates.

tools.name: commsharbor_webhooks
tools.description: List the webhook endpoints of the organization, without their signing secrets.

tools.name: commsharbor_webhook_create
tools.description: Create a webhook and reveal its secret once. Deliveries are signed with timestamped HMAC-SHA256 and retried with exponential backoff; what still fails lands in the tenant-scoped dead-letter queue. Store the secret now — it is never shown again.

tools.name: commsharbor_webhook_get
tools.description: Read one webhook, without its signing secret.

tools.name: commsharbor_webhook_disable
tools.description: Disable a webhook without deleting the evidence of what it already delivered.

tools.name: commsharbor_webhook_deliveries
tools.description: List the signed attempts made to one webhook and their retry state.

tools.name: commsharbor_dead_letters
tools.description: Inspect nominal dead letters. What ended up here after every retry. Records are addressed by opaque ID and carry no recipient PII.

tools.name: commsharbor_dead_letter_replay
tools.description: Replay one campaign or webhook dead letter. One record at a time, addressed explicitly. There is no "replay everything": a bulk replay of an unknown set is how a bad hour becomes a bad day.

tools.name: commsharbor_billing_catalog
tools.description: Read plans, prices and x402 network. Public and unauthenticated: an agent should be able to learn what things cost before deciding whether to sign up at all.

tools.name: commsharbor_billing
tools.description: Read the organization's plan, limits and global entitlements. Read this before a bulk send: `state.active` says whether sending is allowed and `warning` says when the plan runs out. A new organization's trial starts with its first domain or send (`state.started`).

tools.name: commsharbor_billing_purchase
tools.description: Buy a pass or top-up through the house's payment door (credit or x402); 409 while live checkout is off. While `catalog.checkout_live` is false this answers **409 `checkout_disabled`** — nobody is charged by accident; the local dev stack completes it with the house's simulated payment. Otherwise, wit

tools.name: commsharbor_operations
tools.description: List current operational alerts without PII. Covers dead letters, backlog, worker and SNS failures, reputation, paused sending, quota and conservative SES/SNS cost capacity — never with recipient PII.

tools.name: commsharbor_operations_refresh
tools.description: Refresh alerts, quota and capacity observations. The GET reads what was last stored; this goes and looks again. Same distinction as domain verification.

tools.name: commsharbor_data_exports
tools.description: List the tenant data exports, which are retained for seven days.

tools.name: commsharbor_data_export_create
tools.description: Create a seven-day tenant JSON export. Scoped to one organization by construction: an export can never contain another tenant's data.

tools.name: commsharbor_data_export_download
tools.description: Download one tenant-scoped JSON export before it expires.

tools.name: commsharbor_deletion_request
tools.description: Read the latest tenant deletion request. `status: "none"` means no erasure was ever requested — the resource always answers, so a client never has to interpret a 404 as "nothing scheduled".

tools.name: commsharbor_deletion_schedule
tools.description: Schedule tenant erasure after seven days using the exact confirmation phrase. The confirmation phrase must be exactly `delete <organization_id>` — typing the id is the point, so nobody erases the wrong tenant by clicking. Erasure deletes the workspace data in CommsHarbor; the organization itself and

tools.name: commsharbor_deletion_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a scheduled tenant erasure. That is what the seven days are for: after they pass, there is nothing left to cancel.

tools.name: commsharbor_tracking_domain
tools.description: Read the organization's tracking domain, the CNAME it needs and whether the platform actually answers on it. Null when there is none: links then use the shared platform origin. `null` when the organization has none — then every link falls back to the platform origin.

tools.name: commsharbor_tracking_domain_create
tools.description: Register the host that will serve this organization's message links. One per organization; registering never activates it. One per organization, and the host is unique across the platform — two tenants claiming the same name would make link routing ambiguous. Registering does not activate: publish t

tools.name: commsharbor_tracking_domain_verify
tools.description: Probe the host now and store what was seen. The ONLY way to reach `active`, and only after reaching this product on that host — DNS resolving is not enough. The only operation that can move a tracking domain to `active`, and it does so only after reaching this product's own health endpoint ON that h

tools.name: commsharbor_tracking_domain_remove
tools.description: Remove the tracking domain; NEW messages go back to the platform origin. Links already sent keep pointing at the removed host. Links already sent keep pointing at the removed host: this stops NEW messages, not old ones.

tools.name: commsharbor_inboxes
tools.description: List the addresses this organization receives on. Up to 100, newest first. A disabled address stays listed: its history is still readable.

tools.name: commsharbor_inbox_create
tools.description: Create a receiving address on a verified sending domain. Fails with 422 when the domain is not verified: receiving on an unproven domain is relay. The domain must already be `verified` or `active` here — receiving on an unproven domain is relay. For mail to actually arrive, the domain's MX must poin

tools.name: commsharbor_inbox_get
tools.description: Read one receiving address and whether it is still accepting mail.

tools.name: commsharbor_inbox_disable
tools.description: Stop accepting mail at this address. History stays readable — this disables, it never erases. Disables, never erases: mail already received stays readable, because it is the customer's data and losing it is not a cleanup. New mail to the address is dropped and counted.

tools.name: commsharbor_inbox_messages
tools.description: List what arrived at one address, newest first. Summaries only, no body. Summaries only — no body. Read one message to get its text, HTML and headers.

tools.name: commsharbor_inbox_message
tools.description: Read one message: body, chosen headers and `auth`. `from` is text the sender chose; `auth` is the SPF/DKIM/DMARC verdict the receiving edge reached. Decide on `auth`. `auth` is what the receiving edge concluded about SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Treat `from` as text the sender chose: `auth` is the part that

tools.name: commsharbor_inbox_attachment
tools.description: Get a five-minute signed URL for one attachment, by its index in the message. The URL expires; the stored file does not. Two steps on purpose: the URL is what travels to a browser, an agent or a chat, never your credential. It expires in five minutes; the stored object does not expire at all.

tools.name: pricing
tools.description: Current public prices and free allowances; no charge.
